title: Cover again?
topic: Rotas, leave, and training versus service
stem:
You are an F2 doctor on a cardiology and respiratory rotation. Over the past two months you have covered four on-call shifts for your colleague Dr Ross so that she can do paid sessions at a private clinic.

You are tired and your own work is suffering. She asks you to cover another weekend on-call next month.
instruction: Rank in order the following actions in response to this situation (1 = Most appropriate; 5 = Least appropriate).

options.text: Agree to this one shift, and tell her it will be the last.
options.brief: A compromise, but it adds to your fatigue.
options.detailed: This is kind, and setting a limit helps. But you are already tired, so taking on more work isn't ideal. It ranks third.

options.text: Tell her kindly that you can't keep covering her shifts.
options.brief: Protects your wellbeing and is honest with her.
options.detailed: You are tired and your work is suffering. Explaining this honestly lets her make other arrangements. It ranks first.

options.text: Suggest she talks to the rota coordinator about her commitments.
options.brief: Points her to the proper route for planning her work.
options.detailed: If she has regular outside commitments, the rota coordinator can help her plan around them properly. It ranks second because it is helpful but doesn't, on its own, answer her request.

options.text: Agree to cover, then call in sick that weekend.
options.brief: Dishonest, and leaves the rota with a gap at short notice.
options.detailed: This avoids an awkward conversation but leaves the ward without a doctor at short notice. It is the least appropriate option.

options.text: Agree to cover again, to avoid any awkwardness.
options.brief: Continues a pattern that is harming your work.
options.detailed: Avoiding conflict this way keeps adding to your fatigue and may affect your patients.

explanation.issue: This tests whether you can set boundaries with a colleague to protect your wellbeing and your patients.
explanation.keyDetails: You have covered repeatedly. You are tired and your work is suffering. The request is for her private work.
explanation.reasoning: [B] sets a clear boundary, [C] points her to the proper route, and [A] is a reasonable compromise. [E] continues the pattern, and [D] is dishonest and leaves a gap.
explanation.competing: [A] might be fine for someone who wasn't tired. Here, your fatigue is the reason to decline.

references.title: Good medical practice
references.note: Domain 4, looking after your own health so patients are not put at risk.
